displayedInputs.question:
The letters \(P,\) \(Q,\) and \(R\) are entered into a \(20 \times 20\) table according to the pattern shown below. How many \(P\)s, \(Q\)s, and \(R\)s will appear in the completed table?

[Figure 1](attached-image-1)

A regular octahedron has eight equilateral triangle faces with four faces meeting at each vertex. Jun will make the regular octahedron shown in the figure by folding the piece of paper below. Which numbered face will end up to the right of \(Q?\)

[Figure 1](attached-image-2)

An equilateral triangle is placed inside a larger equilateral triangle so that the region between them can be divided into three congruent trapezoids, as shown below. The side length of the inner triangle is \(\frac{2}{3}\) the side length of the larger triangle. What is the ratio of the area of one trapezoid to the area of the inner triangle?

[Figure 1](attached-image-3)

Each square in a \(3 \times 3\) grid is randomly filled with one of the \(4\) shaded-and-unshaded tiles shown below on the right.

[Figure 1](attached-image-4)

What is the probability that the tiling will contain a large shaded diamond in one of the smaller \(2 \times 2\) grids? Below is an example of such a tiling.

[Figure 2](attached-image-5)

Isosceles triangle \(ABC\) has equal side lengths \(AB\) and \(BC.\) In the figures below, segments are drawn parallel to \(\overline{AC}\) so that the shaded portions of \(\triangle ABC\) have the same area. The heights of the two unshaded portions are \(11\) and \(5\) units, respectively. What is the height \(h\) of \(\triangle ABC?\)

[Figure 1](attached-image-6)

Zelda played the Adventures of Math game on August \(1\) and scored \(1700\) points. She continued to play daily over the next \(5\) days. The bar chart below shows the daily change in her score compared to the day before. (For example, Zelda’s score on August \(2\) was \(1700 + 80 = 1780\) points.) What was Zelda’s average score in points over the \(6\) days?

[Figure 1](attached-image-7)

All of the rectangles in the figure below, which is drawn to scale, are similar to the enclosing rectangle. Each number represents the area of the rectangle. What is length \(AB?\)

[Figure 1](attached-image-8)

Let \(\mathcal{K}\) be the kite formed by joining two right triangles with legs \(1\) and \(\sqrt3\) along a common hypotenuse. Eight copies of \(\mathcal{K}\) are used to form the polygon shown below. What is the area of \(\triangle ABC?\)

[Figure 1](attached-image-9)

mappings.rationale: The pattern repeats every three rows. Count complete row blocks by multiplication, then add the contributions from the remaining rows.
mappings.answerReason: Starting from the bottom, each block of three rows contains 20 of each letter. Eighteen rows therefore contribute 120 of each. The remaining two rows contribute 13 Ps, 14 Qs, and 13 Rs, giving totals 133, 134, and 133.

mappings.rationale: The task requires mentally folding a triangular net and tracking which face meets the right edge of Q in the displayed solid.
mappings.answerReason: Label the octahedron's opposite vertex pairs ±x, ±y, ±z, and give Q's apex and left/right base vertices x, y, z. Folding along the strip gives face 1 the vertices x, -y, z. It therefore shares Q's right edge xz and occupies the marked position.

mappings.rationale: The equilateral triangles are similar, so their areas scale as the square of their side-length ratio. The remaining area is split equally among three congruent trapezoids.
mappings.answerReason: Normalize the outer triangle's area to 9. The inner triangle then has area 9·(2/3)² = 4. Each trapezoid has area (9-4)/3 = 5/3, so the requested ratio is (5/3):4 = 5:12.

mappings.rationale: A diamond fixes four tile orientations. The four possible diamonds require different orientations of the shared central tile, so their events are mutually exclusive. Alternatively, fixing the central tile leaves exactly one candidate diamond position.
mappings.answerReason: Each of the four 2×2 positions forms a diamond with probability (1/4)^4 = 1/256. No two can occur together because they require different shaded corners in the central tile. Thus the probability is 4/256 = 1/64.

mappings.rationale: Parallel cuts create similar top triangles, allowing areas to be expressed through squared height ratios. An alternative uses equal unshaded areas and proportional bases in the lower trapezoid.
mappings.answerReason: Relative to the whole triangle, the left shaded area is 1-(11/h)² and the right shaded area is ((h-5)/h)². Equality gives h²-121 = (h-5)², hence 10h = 146 and h = 14.6, which satisfies h > 11.

mappings.rationale: Read the signed changes from the bar chart, reconstruct the daily scores by successive addition and subtraction, then calculate their arithmetic mean.
mappings.answerReason: The six scores are 1700, 1780, 1690, 1680, 1740, and 1700. Their sum is 10290, so the average is 10290/6 = 1715 points.

mappings.rationale: The similar rectangles share a common aspect ratio, allowing for the rotations shown in the scale drawing. Their labeled areas and shared horizontal spans determine that ratio, while the total area determines AB.
mappings.answerReason: Let r = AB/H. The upright area-36 and area-4 rectangles have widths 6/√r and 2/√r. Together they span the area-32 rectangle, whose width is √(32r). Thus 8/√r = √(32r), giving r = √2. The areas sum to 200, so AB = √(200√2) = 10∜8.

mappings.rationale: Each half-kite is a 30°-60°-90° triangle. Its horizontal and vertical offsets determine the base and perpendicular altitude of ABC, after which the triangle-area formula applies.
mappings.answerReason: The two lower pairs of kites give AB = 4√3 cos 30° = 6. The left inward corner is √3 sin 30° above AB, and C is another √3 higher. Thus the altitude is 3√3/2, and the area is (1/2)·6·(3√3/2) = 9√3/2.
